title: Power markets: day-ahead, intraday, baseload and peakload
story: Dana switches the screen from gas to a chart full of small bars, one for each part of tomorrow. *"Gas can wait in a pipe or a tank. Power cannot wait: what is produced must be used in the same second. That is why power has many prices for one single day, and why you must always ask: which hours?"*
objective: I can explain why power is traded for each period of the day, and the difference between day-ahead, intraday, baseload and peakload.

write.heading: 1. Why power is special
write.body: Power is hard to **store** in large amounts. Supply must equal demand at every moment, or the grid fails. So the price can change a lot from one hour to the next. Power is quoted in EUR/MWh, like TTF gas (→ L10), but one MWh delivered at 8 p.m. is not the same product as one MWh at 3 a.m.

write.heading: 2. Day-ahead and intraday
write.body:
- **Day-ahead market**: an auction around midday sets a price for each period of tomorrow. In Europe the periods are now 15 minutes.
- **Intraday market**: trading continues until shortly before delivery, to fix last changes (a plant stops, the wind drops).

write.heading: 3. Baseload and peakload
write.body:
- **Baseload**: the same power every hour of the day, 24 hours.
- **Peakload**: power only in busy hours, typically 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays.
Example (illustrative): baseload 90 EUR/MWh, peakload 110 EUR/MWh. Peak is usually dearer because demand is higher.

write.heading: 4. Middle office check
write.body: Volume = MW × hours. Example: 10 MW baseload for one day = 10 × 24 = 240 MWh. Peak hours are fewer, so always check the hours before the volume (→ L4). Power plants sit in the middle of the value chain (→ L3).

check.q: Why can the power price change so much from hour to hour?
check.a: Power is hard to store, so supply must equal demand at every moment. Each hour (or quarter-hour) has its own balance and its own price.

check.q: What is the difference between baseload and peakload?
check.a: Baseload is the same power every hour, 24 hours a day. Peakload is power only in busy hours, typically 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays.

check.q: A trade is 5 MW baseload for one day. What volume in MWh?

read_more: In Europe, the day-ahead power markets of most countries are coupled in one daily auction (Single Day-Ahead Coupling, SDAC), run by power exchanges such as EPEX SPOT and Nord Pool. Since delivery day 1 October 2025, this auction prices 15-minute periods instead of hours. Exact peak hours depend on the market and the contract, so middle office always reads the product definition. Sources: EPEX SPOT news, 'Successful implementation of 15-minute MTU in SDAC' (October 2025).
